title: The gate never hits Go's test cache: it runs in a fresh worktree every time
description:
MEASURED, 2026-09-20. Two worktrees of the SAME commit:

    worktree A, first run    ok internal/schema 0.309s   ok internal/runfeed 0.406s
    worktree A, second run   ok internal/schema (cached) ok internal/runfeed (cached)
    worktree B, same commit  ok internal/schema 0.311s   ok internal/runfeed 0.427s

Go's test cache keys on the files a test opened, by ABSOLUTE PATH. repoGit.tempWorktree makes a fresh directory under the system temp dir for every gate (/var/folders/.../ticfac-gate-<random>/tree), so every gate is worktree B: a cold cache, every package re-run from scratch, every tick.

The cost is the whole gate. On a quiet host the go half is ~6 minutes wall and ~500s of CPU across packages (herdr 176s, runstate 113s, subprocess 74s, cli 49s, factory 43s). Under contention it has taken 32, 37, 78 and 105 minutes today. NONE of that work is necessary for a tick that touched one package.

It also means the operator's decision on 2026-09-18 to drop -count=1 — explicitly so 'a package whose inputs are unchanged answers from cache' — has bought NOTHING. The reasoning was right and the mechanism was already broken; the note in .tick/runners.toml describing that saving is describing something that never happened.

Fix: run the gate in a STABLE directory per repository rather than a fresh temp one — reset it to the target commit each time (git reset --hard, git clean -xdff) so it is still a clean tree, but at a path the cache recognises. Most ticks would then gate in seconds.

Two things to get right:
- Contamination: a reused directory must be reset hard enough that a previous gate cannot influence this one. That is the property the fresh worktree was buying, and it must be kept by construction, not by hope.
- Concurrency: two gates in one checkout must not share the stable directory. Key it by run id or take a lock — and see w1j, since serialising gates on a host is wanted anyway.

Related: mbv (the caching soundness caveat, which is about absolute-path READS and is the same mechanism seen from the other side), w1j (host contention), 9pz (which made the gate stop blocking the loop — this makes it stop taking six minutes).
acceptance_criteria: A gate on a tree whose packages are unchanged answers from Go's test cache, measured; a reused gate directory cannot carry state between gates; and two concurrent gates in one checkout do not share it
